notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Connect the portfolio to the right commercial relationship.
intro: A proposed GTM operations workbench for Rentana: map owners, operators and properties before enriching accounts, building audiences or assigning pipeline ownership.
queueIntro: All companies and portfolio relationships are fictional. No tenant records, rent recommendations, housing eligibility or property-level pricing decisions appear here.
workbenchIntro: Review the business relationship and audience rules. The demo supports software sales operations, not rental pricing or housing decisions.
firstBuild: A clean operator record with explicit exclusions
firstBody: Resolve ownership and management relationships, preserve current account books and return import-ready research with a clear stage and next action.

fields.label: Owner, operator and property relationships mapped
Portfolio scope has a current source
Revenue, asset or operating buyer role supported
Territory and book ownership rules reconciled
Audience exclusions and existing customers checked
Stage evidence and next action recorded

rules.title: Resolve the real-estate account structure
rules.next: A property owner, third-party manager and operating brand can be different entities. Preserve the relationship graph.

rules.title: Verify the portfolio context
rules.next: Do not turn a stale property count or acquisition rumor into a current account fact.

rules.title: Find the relevant business role
rules.next: Connect the portfolio question to the person responsible for the operating workflow.

rules.title: Resolve account assignment
rules.next: Check the parent relationship and existing book before assigning a new property-level lead.

rules.title: Apply the audience exclusions
rules.next: Keep customers, active opportunities and stopped contacts out of an unrelated new-logo sequence.

rules.title: Make the pipeline stage inspectable
rules.next: Record the business milestone, next step and receiving owner rather than relying on a filled stage field.

ready.title: Ready for an operator-account review
ready.next: The seller can review the relationship graph and operating question. Audience enrollment and production CRM updates remain separate reviewed actions.

experiments.name: Relationship-aware enrichment
experiments.hypothesis: Mapping owner and operator separately reduces misrouted accounts.
experiments.primary: Correct account assignments per reviewed record
experiments.guardrail: False merges and duplicate parent accounts
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Exclusions before audience expansion
experiments.hypothesis: A maintained exclusion contract improves campaign quality.
experiments.guardrail: Existing customers added to cold outreach
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Define the account and territory model
roadmap.body: Partner with Sales, Marketing and CS on owner/operator relationships, book assignment and stage criteria.

roadmap.title: Build clean, import-ready records
roadmap.body: Pilot sourced enrichment, validation and living audience exclusions. Make failed records easy to inspect and correct.

roadmap.title: Turn support requests into better systems
roadmap.body: Use repeated CRM questions to prioritize structural fixes. Maintain dashboards and train the team on operating definitions.
roadmap.measure: Pipeline hygiene, repeat issues and team adoption

metricsTitle: Clean records are a maintained operating system.
metricsIntro: Synthetic audit of one hundred business records.
metricsNotes: These invented records do not describe Rentana’s customers or production CRM.
A property count is not a unique account count. Preserve entity-level denominators.

aiApplication: At Rentana, I would use coordinated research agents to resolve owner-manager relationships and explicit exclusions before an import proposal. The loop would preserve current account books, validate duplicates and measure accepted records and useful next actions.
